To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a heuristic for energy-balanced task allocation on wireless sensor networks with dynamic voltage scaling, which achieves a performance improvement of 120% - 250% compared with the case without voltage scaling.
we have developed an efficient ILP formulation and a 3-phase heuristic to solve the energy-balanced task allocation problem.

we have developed an ILP-based and a heuristic approach for the problem of energy-balanced task allocation in networked embedded system, and the experimental results show that for the large scale problems, using our approaches, the system lifetime can be improved by 120-250% compared with the case when no voltage scaling is employed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of energy-efficient allocation of periodic applications onto a set of networked elements.
the problem of task allocation for energy-balanced collaborative processing of periodic applications in networked embedded system, where the time and energy costs are considered.
the problem of energy-balanced task allocation and scheduling in networked embedded real-time systems.

this work is an important contribution to energy-balanced task allocation in networked embedded real-time systems.
the proposed approaches are efficient and effective for solving the energy-balanced task allocation problem in networked embedded system with dynamic voltage scaling.
this paper provides a novel and effective approach to energy-efficient task allocation for collaborative real-time applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach is the first one that considers the energy-balanced allocation of real-time tasks onto networked embedded systems with dynamic voltage scaling.
we provide a systematic approach for solving the problem of energy-balanced task allocation with respect to the energy of the elements.
the heuristic approach can be applied for a variety of problems with a large number of tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by considering the energy-balanced task allocation, the system lifetime can be improved by 50-300\% compared with the case when no energy-balanced allocation is performed.
energy balancing can be used as a powerful technique to improve the lifetime of networked embedded systems.
by exploiting the energy-latency relationship in both computation and communication, the system lifetime of a networked embedded system can be significantly improved.
